products.heading: Our Insurance Products
products.intro: Every policy is explained clearly. Every recommendation is honest. Nothing is rushed.

p1.name: Term Life Insurance
p1.body: Term life insurance provides affordable, straightforward coverage for a defined period — typically 10, 20, or 30 years. If you pass away during the term, your family receives a tax-free lump sum death benefit to replace your income, pay off debts, and maintain their quality of life. It is the most cost-effective way to get significant coverage during the years your family depends on you most. Ideal for young families, new homeowners, and anyone with financial dependents.
p1.imageAlt: A young couple stand close together in a sunlit grassy field at golden hour, gently holding and kissing their baby.

p2.name: Final Expense Insurance
p2.body: Final expense insurance is a small whole life policy — typically between $5,000 and $25,000 — written to meet the costs a family faces immediately after a death: the service, outstanding medical bills, and the administration that follows. The premium is level for the life of the policy and the benefit amount does not reduce over time. No medical exam is required for most applicants between ages 50 and 85. It is the most compassionate gift you can leave your family — the certainty that they will never carry that financial burden alone.
p2.imageAlt: A silver-haired woman in a mint-green polka-dot dress laughs over her shoulder against a cream wall with greenery behind her.

p3.name: Mortgage Protection Insurance
p3.body: Mortgage protection is designed to keep your family in their home if you are no longer there to make the payments. If you pass away, become disabled, or face a critical illness, the policy pays off your remaining mortgage balance directly — so your family is not forced out of the home you built together. Unlike PMI, which protects the lender, mortgage protection protects your family. It is one of the most targeted and powerful forms of protection a homeowner can carry.
p3.imageAlt: A couple in coats stand on the wooden porch of their house beside stacked moving boxes as one of them unlocks the front door with a key.

p4.name: Indexed Universal Life (IUL)
p4.body: Indexed Universal Life insurance is permanent coverage that builds real cash value linked to a stock market index — such as the S&P 500 — while a policy floor means index losses are not credited against the value you have built. Your money grows when markets rise and stays flat when they fall. The cash value grows tax-deferred, can be accessed tax-free through policy loans, and the death benefit lasts your entire lifetime. IUL is the preferred vehicle for entrepreneurs, business owners, and professionals who want life insurance that works as a long-term financial strategy.
p4.imageAlt: A silver-haired couple hold coffee cups in the open doorway of their home, a snow-covered deck behind them.

p5.name: Fixed Indexed Annuities (FIAs)
p5.body: A Fixed Indexed Annuity is a retirement vehicle that grows your money based on market index performance — with a floor that means index losses are not credited against your principal. Your account is credited based on the performance of a market index, without being invested in the market directly. FIAs offer lifetime income options, tax-deferred growth, and a death benefit that passes to your beneficiaries. Designed for pre-retirees and retirees who want index-linked crediting alongside a predictable income floor.
p5.imageAlt: A smiling older couple stand outdoors among sunlit trees; the man in a straw hat holds a phone as the woman rests a hand on his shoulder.

p6.name: Medicare Insurance
p6.body: Navigating Medicare can be overwhelming — but it does not have to be. Synergy Insurance Group helps individuals turning 65 and existing Medicare beneficiaries understand their options and select the right plan. We work with multiple Medicare carriers to compare Medicare Supplement (Medigap) plans, Medicare Advantage plans, and Medicare Part D prescription drug coverage. Our agents simplify the process, explain every option in plain language, and help you choose the coverage that fits your health needs and your budget — at no additional cost to you.
p6.imageAlt: A silver-haired woman in glasses smiles while holding a basket of freshly picked celery and tomatoes in a sunny vegetable garden.

p7.name: Health Insurance
p7.body: Access to quality health insurance is one of the most important decisions you can make for yourself and your family. Synergy Insurance Group works with multiple health insurance carriers to help individuals, families, and self-employed professionals find plans that provide real coverage at a price that makes sense. Whether you need an ACA marketplace plan, a short-term health plan, or a supplemental health policy to fill gaps in your existing coverage, our licensed agents walk you through every option in plain language, and leave the decision with you.
p7.imageAlt: A mother, father, and young child make dumplings together at a bright kitchen counter set with eggs and flour.

b1.name: Tax-free is three different things
b1.body:
The word tax-free appears three times in the product list above, and it is not the same mechanism on any of the three occasions.

The first is the death benefit. When a term life policy pays, the lump sum your family receives is not counted as income to them. That is what the description above means by a tax-free lump sum death benefit: the benefit is not reduced on its way through a tax return, which is why it can be sized against the debts and the income it is meant to replace rather than against some fraction of itself.

The second is accumulation. An Indexed Universal Life policy carries a cash value alongside its death benefit, and the list above describes that value as growing tax-deferred. Deferred is a narrower word than free. It means no tax falls due in the years the value rises, because nothing has come out of the contract yet.

The third is access, and it is where the two previous ideas meet. The list above says the cash value can be accessed tax-free through policy loans. A loan is not a withdrawal. Money borrowed against the cash value is not treated as income received, which is the whole reason the loan structure is used instead of simply taking the money out.

Two consequences belong next to that loan rather than in a footnote. A loan still outstanding when the policy pays is settled out of the death benefit, so what reaches your family is reduced by what was borrowed and by the interest that has accrued on it. And a policy that ends with a loan still standing against it can leave a bill behind instead of a benefit.

Three mechanisms, one word. Which applies depends on the product and on which part of it you are touching.

b2.name: What a floor does, and what it does not
b2.body:
A floor is the single mechanic that makes an indexed product behave unlike an investment, and reading it narrowly is the only way to understand what you are buying.

Begin with what the money is not doing. In an Indexed Universal Life policy or a Fixed Indexed Annuity, your money is not in the market. It is with the carrier, and the carrier credits interest to it according to the movement of a market index — the S&P 500 is the one named above. You do not hold the index. You hold a contract whose crediting rate is calculated from how that index moved.

The floor governs the downside of that calculation. If the index falls, the crediting rate does not go negative, and the index loss is not credited against the value you have already built. That is the whole of the mechanic. In the words used above, your money grows when markets rise and stays flat when they fall.

Two things follow that are worth saying out loud. A flat year is not a frozen year, because a life insurance contract has its own internal charges and those do not stop when crediting does. And a floor never travels alone: the same contract that limits how far a falling index can reach you also limits how much of a rising one is credited to you.

b3.name: A period, or a lifetime
b3.body:
Two of the seven products are the same idea sold on opposite terms, and the comparison table puts the whole difference in one column. Term life reads 10-30 years under Duration. Indexed Universal Life reads Lifetime.

A term policy is a defined-period contract. You choose the length — ten, twenty and thirty years are named above as the usual ones — and across that stretch the insurer carries the risk. If the term runs out and you are still here, the contract ends with it and nothing is paid. That is not a flaw in the product. It is the reason the product is priced the way it is, and it is why term is described above as the most cost-effective way to get significant coverage.

A permanent policy is not written against a period at all. The death benefit, as described above, lasts your entire lifetime, and a contract sold on those terms is priced on the expectation of eventually paying. What the higher price buys, besides duration, is the next column across: Cash Value, which reads Yes for Indexed Universal Life and No for term.

The choice is therefore less about which product is better than about which question you are answering. Term answers what happens to a household if the earner is not there across the years it is still being built. Permanent answers what should be in place whenever that turns out to be, and holds a value inside the contract while it waits.

b4.name: The medical exam column
b4.body:
The comparison table carries a column most people are too polite to ask about directly. Under Medical Exam, three of the seven products read No and two read Sometimes. Nothing reads Always, and that absence is doing real work.

Sometimes is the honest answer for term life and for Indexed Universal Life, and it is honest precisely because it declines to commit either way. Whether an exam is called for is a decision the carrier makes about a particular application, not a fixed property of the product.

No is the answer for final expense, and there it is a design decision rather than a concession. The wording above is specific: no medical exam is required for most applicants between ages 50 and 85. Read that against the age range the same table gives the product — 50 to 85 — and the reason is plain. An exam requirement would sit directly across the entrance of the product for exactly the people it was built for.

What none of this means is that health stops mattering. It means the question is put in a different form. An exam is one way of asking it; a set of questions on an application is another, and the answers given there carry the same weight in deciding whether the policy is offered and on what terms. The column is telling you which method the product uses, not whether your health is being considered.

b5.name: When a balance becomes a payment
b5.body:
The annuity row is the only one in the table whose Duration does not describe how long you are covered. It reads Lifetime income, and that phrasing is precise. The other six products name a period across which something would be paid on an event. This one names a period across which something is paid on a schedule.

The product has two halves. In the first, money goes in and interest is credited — for a Fixed Indexed Annuity, credited from the movement of a market index, on the same floor mechanic described above, and deferred from tax for as long as it stays inside the contract. In the second, that accumulated balance is turned into a stream of payments.

That conversion is the entire point of the product, and it is what is meant above by lifetime income options. Options, in the plural, is the operative word: the conversion can be made in more than one way, and the ways differ in how large each payment is and how long the payments continue. Those two quantities move against each other.

One thing the table has no column for is worth adding here. The description above notes that a Fixed Indexed Annuity also carries a death benefit that passes to your beneficiaries, which means a balance that was never converted into payments is not left stranded by the fact that the conversion never happened.

The table gives the product an age range of 45 to 70, which describes its shape well. It is bought across the years income is still arriving, to matter across the years when it is not.

offer.heading: What joining actually involves.
offer.body: Four things Synergy provides. Everything after that is the work itself.

i.label: Leads you do not have to buy
i.body: Synergy runs its own lead generation, so you are not buying lists or working a cold phone book. The people you speak to have already put their hand up and asked someone to call them back, which changes the first ten seconds of every conversation you have.

ii.label: Licensing, supported
ii.body: You do not need an insurance background to start. Florida licensing is a state exam with a published syllabus, and someone at Synergy walks you through what it covers, what the state asks for, and the carrier paperwork that follows it. You are not left to decode it alone.

iii.label: Training that keeps going
iii.body: Training here is not a first-week orientation you never see again. Sessions run on a regular schedule, they cover live cases rather than theory, and the people running them are the same people you work alongside the rest of the week.

iv.label: An Orlando team, in person
iv.body: The office is on Major Boulevard and the team actually works from it. If you want people to learn from in the same room — someone to sit in on a call, or to ask why a case was declined — that is what this is, rather than a contract and a login.

one.heading: Get in Touch
one.body: Call the office or send the contact form. It is a short conversation, not an application: where you are now, whether you already hold a licence, and what you are hoping the work will look like. Nobody is going to push you toward a decision on a first call, and you will speak to someone who actually works here rather than a recruiter reading from a script. If it is plainly not a fit, we will say so then, because wasting six weeks of your time helps neither of us.

two.heading: Meet the Team
two.body: Before anything is signed you come and meet the people you would be working with. You see the office, you sit in on how a case is actually worked, and you ask the questions that are hard to ask over the phone. This is deliberately a two-way conversation: Synergy is deciding whether to invest training time in you, and you are deciding whether these are people you want to learn the business from. Both answers matter and both are allowed to be no.

three.heading: Get Licensed
three.body: Florida requires a life insurance licence before you can sell, so that is the first real milestone. You are pointed at the pre-licensing course, the state exam and the fingerprinting the state asks for, and once you pass, the carrier appointments and the paperwork behind them are handled with you rather than handed to you. It is the part most people expect to be the obstacle, and it is mostly a matter of doing the steps in the right order.

four.heading: Get Appointed & Start Selling
four.body: You begin sitting with real clients, with someone experienced alongside you for the first ones. You will not be handed a phone list and wished luck. Early appointments are reviewed afterwards — what was asked, what was missed, what the carrier came back with — and that review is the part that turns a licence into competence. The support does not stop once you are producing; it changes shape.

cta.heading: Come and talk to us.
cta.body: There is no application form on this page. The first step is a conversation, and the phone and the contact form both reach the same Orlando office.

opening.phrase: You are not buying a job.
opening.imageAlt: Five Synergy agents standing together for a portrait against a light studio wall.
opening.lead: Most people who ask about this work have already been sold something once. So here is the plain version, before anyone asks you for a phone number.
opening.a1: You sit with families and explain products that are genuinely hard to read: term, final expense, indexed universal life, annuities. Most of the job is listening carefully, asking better questions than the last person did, and being willing to say that a product is wrong for someone. The paperwork is learnable in weeks. The judgement takes longer, and it is the part that makes the difference to the person across the table.
opening.a2: Leads generated in-house rather than bought from a list broker, so the people you call have asked to hear from someone. Licensing support, because most people arriving here have never sat a state exam. Training on a regular schedule, run by the people you work beside rather than by a course somebody sells you. And an office in Orlando where those people actually are.
opening.a3: Turning up, mostly. Licensing is a state exam with a published syllabus and it does not pass itself. Early appointments are uncomfortable, and the only way through that is doing enough of them with someone experienced sitting in. If you want something that pays without being learned, this is the wrong room, and we would rather say so now than six weeks in.

range.heading: What you would be selling.
range.body: Synergy is not a one-product shop, and that matters more than it sounds. When the only policy you hold is the wrong one for the person across the table, the conversation has nowhere honest left to go. These are the lines Synergy writes. Working out which one a family actually needs — and saying so when the answer is none of them — is most of the skill.

portal.metaDescription: Licensing, contracting and carrier reference for Synergy agents.
portal.heading: Welcome to the Synergy Insurance Portal
portal.subhead: Everything you need to get licensed, get contracted and get appointed with our carriers. The sections run in order — each one assumes the one above it is done.

licensing.heading: Licensing checklist
licensing.intro: Your route to a resident insurance licence. Take these in order — each step depends on the one before it.

s1.heading: Check what your resident state requires
s1.body: Licensing is set state by state. Study hours, the exam itself, the fees and whether you need fingerprints all differ. Confirm your own state's rules before you spend anything.

s2.heading: Enrol in a pre-licensing course
s2.body: Register on a desktop or laptop rather than a phone. These enrolment forms are long and they routinely fail on mobile browsers, and a half-completed registration is a problem you have to unpick before you can start studying.

s3.heading: Book the state exam while you are still studying
s3.body: About two-thirds of the way through the course, book your exam. A booked date is a deadline, and a deadline is what gets a course finished. Check your testing provider, your nearest centre and whether a background check is required.
s3.link1: Xcel Solutions — exam and licensing requirements

s4.heading: Send us your exam date
s4.body: Forward the confirmation from the testing provider, or send a screenshot of the booking. Put “Exam date confirmed” and your name in the subject line so it is filed against your record.

s5.heading: Tell us the moment you pass
s5.body: Let the admin team and your team leader know as soon as you have your result. That is what starts the contracting stage, and nothing moves until we hear from you.

s6.heading: Get fingerprinted, if your state asks for it
s6.body: Some states run a background check before they will issue a licence. If yours does, book it as early as you can — results often take longer to come back than the exam result does. The state links in step one tell you whether it applies and who is approved to take them.

s7.heading: Apply for your resident licence
s7.body: The testing centre usually explains how to apply once you have passed. Fees and additional checks vary, so call your state Department of Insurance if anything is unclear. Contracting cannot begin until the licence is issued and your producer number exists.

s8.heading: Collect your National Producer Number
s8.body: There is nothing to apply for. Your NPN is created automatically when your state reports the approved licence to the national registry. Chase your state department daily if it is slow, then look the number up here once it lands.

licensing.done: Licensed. Work through the contracting checklist next.

contracting.heading: New agent checklist
contracting.intro: Getting appointed with carriers. In order again — the document step assumes everything above it is finished.

c1.heading: Buy errors and omissions cover
c1.body: Buy E&O from whichever provider you prefer, and shop around. Two conditions are not negotiable.
c1.rule1: Cover of at least $1M per claim and $3M in aggregate.
c1.rule2: The policy must start on the first of the current month. If today is 12 April, the start date is 1 April. A policy that begins on the first of next month stops contracting and onboarding until that date arrives.

c2.heading: Complete an anti-money-laundering course
c2.body: Every carrier wants a current AML certificate before it will appoint you. The course runs about an hour, costs very little, and the certificate lasts two years. One certificate from a recognised provider is normally accepted widely, although a few carriers insist on their own version. Keep the completion certificate — it is attached in the next step.

c3.heading: Send your documents in one email
c3.body: Attach all five items to a single message. Use the subject line “Ready to contract” followed by your name. Documents sent separately get processed separately, which is slower for you.
c3.doc2: National Producer Number, as it appears on NIPR

c4.heading: Prepare a voided check — but do not email it
c4.body: Carriers set up payment to you directly, which is why they need your banking details. Save a PDF of a voided check ready for the onboarding call. A voided check is strongly preferred. Failing that, a letter on bank letterhead signed by a bank representative showing your routing number, account number and personal details will do, as will a direct-deposit printout that shows your name, routing number and account number.
c4.warn: Do not send this by email. Bring it to the onboarding call.

c5.heading: Have these ready for the onboarding call
c5.body: The call is held over video. Have the following to hand so it can be finished in one sitting.
c5.item1: Your bank's name, address and phone number — any branch is fine.
c5.item2: Your beneficiary's full name, Social Security number and email address. The beneficiary must be over 18 and legally present in the United States.

c6.heading: Finish the required product training
c6.body: Indexed universal life and annuity carriers will not appoint you until the product training is complete. Do it straight after onboarding and send the admin team a screenshot of your completion screen.

after.heading: After you send your documents
after.body: The admin team will be in touch to book your onboarding and contracting call over video.
